solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very old ruined city containing Etruria's first arena

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very

indicators.note: something ruined has been knocked out of shape, so these letters lose their original order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the shuffled group

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the ancient Italian region
the crossword's favourite city

explanation.surface: A tour of an ancient Etruscan ruin, with its crumbling amphitheatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing' only tells you the E joins the three letters of 'old' before they are rearranged. The surface's 'arena' sounds Roman and ancient, but the answer is a modern cycling track.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is a banked track stadium built for cycle racing, a specific kind of sporting venue.

clue.text: Man runs away from rascally fellow

indicators.note: something sent away from a place is no longer in it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: an archaic word for a rogue or knave
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A man flees from a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a verb-sounding noun here: a man is a manservant, as in 'my man will see to it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a gentleman's personal servant, and 'man' is an old word for such a male attendant.

clue.text: Barcelona: King OK following surgery drama

indicators.note: after an operation things have been cut and rearranged, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical bulletin: a Barcelona king is fine after his operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the first three words is used. The title is John Osborne's 1956 play that launched the 'angry young men' of British theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Look Back in Anger is a famous stage play by John Osborne, so it is an example of a drama.

clue.text: Awful-sounding clan abuse

indicators.note: how a phrase sounds rather than how it is spelt is what matters here

parts.note: dire means dreadful
a tribe is a clan or kinship group

explanation.surface: A family group's insults that sound horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'dire tribe' matches the answer, especially in a non-rhotic British accent where the R of dire is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, so it is a form of abuse delivered in words.

clue.text: Stubborn old bishop rude at turns

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: letters that turn about end up facing new positions, so their order changes

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cantankerous elderly bishop who is impolite from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At turns' reads like 'at times', but 'turns' is acting on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate describes someone who refuses to change their mind, a close synonym for obstinate or unyielding.

clue.text: Increase the wealth of Henri Charrière, somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means only partly, so just a portion of the words is used

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the first and last names

explanation.surface: Did the prison memoir make its author a bit richer?
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Charrière wrote Papillon, his best-selling account of escaping a French penal colony, which did indeed make him wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich someone is to make them richer, a direct verb equivalent of the definition phrase.

clue.text: Bloke coming across mile title holder

indicators.note: to come across something is to straddle it, so one piece spans another

parts.note: chap is informal British for a man
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: A runner who covers a mile and holds a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The athletics picture tempts you toward a runner; the mile is only a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Champ is a casual shortening of champion, the person currently holding a sporting title.

clue.text: Smuggled in Charlie, New York crack

indicators.note: something put in sits inside a surrounding pair

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Cocaine smuggled into New York, with crack too.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie and crack both suggest drugs, but Charlie is a letter and crack is a small gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a narrow opening or chink in a wall, so a crack in the physical sense.

clue.text: For engineering, lay a main central Tube

indicators.note: engineering means constructing or rebuilding, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Engineering advice about laying a central pipe, or a new London Underground line.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T tempts a reading as the London Underground, known as the Tube; it is just a body passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canal is the long digestive passage from mouth to anus, anatomically a tube.

clue.text: Corral fierce woman, an old warrior chief

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
a dragon is a formidable, aggressive woman

explanation.surface: Rounding up a ferocious woman, a tribal warlord of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corral' looks like a verb acting on the woman, but it simply supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendragon was a title for a supreme leader among the ancient Britons, borne by Uther, King Arthur's father.

clue.text: Fat misshapen toe's torn gym clothing

indicators.note: having torn something means splitting it open, so one piece gets wedged into another

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: misshapen means twisted out of form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A deformed toe has ripped through someone's gym kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Fat [that a] misshapen toe has torn': the rearranged toe splits the fat in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is the close-fitting one-piece garment worn by gymnasts and dancers.

clue.text: Spanish football side, big guns regularly failing, change formation

parts.note: as in Real Madrid or Real Sociedad

indicators.note: letters failing at regular intervals means every other one drops out

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters survive

explanation.surface: A Spanish club whose star players keep missing must change tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change formation' fits the football story perfectly, which disguises that it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to arrange again in a new line or grouping, the same idea as reshaping a formation.

clue.text: Italian banker having billions in bank?

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a bank of seats or controls is a tier, a row
B is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: An Italian financier with billions in his bank.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, the thing that has banks. Here the bank of the wordplay is a row, not a financial one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river flowing through Rome; as a river it has banks, making it a cryptic 'banker'.

clue.text: Tory interrupting judge, extremely unpopular storyteller

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

parts.note: to rate is to assess or judge
Con is short for Conservative

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends

parts.note: first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A Conservative heckles a judge and proves very unpopular.
explanation.walkthrough: Judge is a verb here, not a person in a wig. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone who tells anecdotes skilfully and entertainingly, a teller of tales.

clue.text: Be denigrating rugby player, part European

parts.note: a back is one of the rear positions in a rugby team
a bit is a part or piece
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Insulting a rugby player who is partly European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part European' reads as one idea, but 'part' and 'European' supply separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To backbite is to speak spitefully about someone behind their back, a way of running them down.

clue.text: Rely on report perhaps of Kent financial officer

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: a report is a sound, like a gunshot, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: Clark Kent is Superman's everyday identity

explanation.surface: Trusting a news report about a finance official from the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent looks like the English county; it is Clark Kent's surname. In British English clerk is pronounced 'clark', so the sound matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank clerk is an employee handling money and accounts at a bank, loosely an officer of finance.

clue.text: Second day at the Biergarten, just for men

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Tag is German for day

explanation.surface: The second day at a German beer garden is a men-only session.
explanation.walkthrough: The Biergarten tells you the word for day is German.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag describes an event for men only, as in a stag party held for a groom before his wedding.

clue.text: Christians of note on street in Rolls

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a bap is a soft British bread roll
the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Musical churchgoers driving down the road in a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts one piece directly after another; the capital R makes Rolls look like the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptists are members of a Protestant denomination practising adult baptism, so a group of Christians.

clue.text: California cops wearing symbol of rank in a casual manner

indicators.note: whoever is wearing something is inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a sash worn across the body can mark rank or office
the Los Angeles Police Department

explanation.surface: West Coast police wearing their insignia carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The adverb sense matters for the swap: slapdash can mean hastily and carelessly as well as careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Done slapdash means done hurriedly and carelessly, without proper attention or effort.

clue.text: Green supporter rejected importing iodine

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back the way it came
to import is to bring something inside

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: An environmentalist backer turned down because of iodine imports.
explanation.walkthrough: Green suggests ecology here, but it means inexperienced; the answer is an adjective form of naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif means naive or unsophisticated, and green is a common idiom for inexperienced or gullible.

clue.text: Hag having energy cut off acquires old Scottish kettle

indicators.note: to acquire is to take something in
cutting something off removes it from the end

parts.note: a crone is an ugly old woman
E is the symbol for energy
auld is Scots for old

explanation.surface: A witch who has lost her power gets a Scottish cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The hag and the kettle conjure Macbeth's witches, and the answer is just what they stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is a large metal cooking pot, and kettle in its older sense is any such pot for boiling.

clue.text: Encourage ship's doctor, having not succeeded

indicators.note: not having something means it has been taken away

parts.note: a naval or ship's doctor is a surgeon
S is the genealogy abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Cheer on a ship's medic after a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not succeeded' reads as failing, but it means losing the letter for succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge on is to spur someone forward with encouragement, a phrasal verb meaning the same as encourage.

clue.text: Mum's drunk the setter's very large cocktail

indicators.note: whatever is drunk goes inside the drinker

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
the setter is I, so the setter's is 'I'm'
OS is the clothing size outsize

explanation.surface: Mother has downed the crossword compiler's enormous mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Mum has drunk': the apostrophe-s is 'has', joining the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimosa is a mixed drink of champagne and orange juice, the American name for a Buck's Fizz.

clue.text: Switzerland with supplies flown in as aid for people in the mountains

definitions.text: aid for people in the mountains

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
an airlift is a delivery of supplies by aircraft

explanation.surface: Swiss relief supplies dropped by air to stranded mountain villagers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a humanitarian rescue; the 'aid' is a ski-slope machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairlift carries skiers and walkers up slopes on suspended seats, helping people get around mountain resorts.

clue.text: Fussy and irritable, looking neither to right nor (later) left

indicators.text: looking neither to right nor (later) left
indicators.note: having neither of two things means both are missing

parts.note: prickly means touchy or easily irritated
R is the abbreviation for right
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A cantankerous person who refuses to look either way when crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: '(Later)' points out that the letter for left comes later in the word than the one for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Picky means hard to please and overly selective, an informal synonym for fussy or choosy.

clue.text: Years and years working in flipping outer space!

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it
to flip something is to turn it over so it faces the other way

parts.note: the sky is the space above
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A fed-up astronaut complains about spending ages working in bloody space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word; it is the turnaround signal. Yonks is British slang for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is informal British slang for a very long time, as in 'I haven't seen her for ages'.

clue.text: Painter: knighted composer — not a writer from Italy

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to take out the letter that follows

parts.note: Sir Edward Elgar, English composer
taken as written, the letter removed
Umberto Eco, author of The Name of the Rose

explanation.surface: A gallery guide: a painter, a knighted composer, and a pointed note that no Italian author is included.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'not a writer from Italy' look like one negative phrase, but 'not a' acts on the composer and the writer simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born Renaissance artist who worked in Spain, famous for elongated figures.

clue.text: River sparkled endlessly, with woman taking dip

indicators.note: to take a dip is to plunge into something, so one piece goes inside
without its end, a word loses its final letter

parts.note: shone means gleamed or sparkled
a common crossword woman's name

explanation.surface: A sparkling river where a woman goes for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shannon is Ireland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon flows through the middle of Ireland, so it is an example of a river.

clue.text: Thai people live in the outskirts of Kingston

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters count

parts.note: first and last letters
to be is to exist or live, and 'are' is a form of it

explanation.surface: Thai migrants live on the edge of Kingston.
explanation.walkthrough: The Karen are an ethnic group of the Thai-Burmese border hills; the name is not the Western first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Karen are a hill people living in Myanmar and western Thailand, so a people found in Thailand.

clue.text: Patriarch of drama school in Yale cast you and me

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it
metal cast in a mould is given a new form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Sch is the abbreviation for school
you and I together are us

explanation.surface: A drama school at Yale casting a show starring the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' fits the theatre picture, which hides its job of rearranging the university's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschylus, the earliest of the great Athenian tragedians, is often called the father of tragedy.
